Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

reason noun

the power of thought

classical

Cic. Off. 1.101: ut ratiō praesit, appetītus obtemperet
M-O s.v. reason
Traupman 368

ratiō, ratiōnis f.

noun, third declension

reason, the reasoning mind

What sets a human being apart: homō autem, quod ratiōnis est particeps (Cic. Off. 1.11).

Other words

  • mēns, mentis f. — the mind, understanding, judgment

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Tusc. 3.11: mentis, cui rēgnum tōtīus animī ā nātūrā tribūtum est

Examples

  • ita fit, ut ratiō praesit, appetītus obtemperet

    so it comes about that reason leads and appetite obeysCic. Off. 1.101

See also reason, idea.

SourcesLewis & Short: ratio · Lewis & Short: mens

Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. reason.
